chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-ʿAbbas ibn Maʿruf, from ʿAli ibn Mahziyar, from Hammad ibn ʿIsa and Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Muʿawiyah ibn ʿAmmar, who said:
I asked Aba ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام about a menstruating woman who sweats in her clothes: may she perform salat (prayer) in them before washing them? He said: “Yes, there is no harm.”

As for the report narrated by al-Husayn ibn Saʿid, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn ʿAmmar, who said: I said to Abi ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, “The menstruating woman sweats in her garment.” He said: “She washes it.” I said: “If beneath the shift there is a waist-wrapper, and the sweat only reaches what is below the waist-wrapper?” He said: “She does not wash it.”

This means when some filth has affected it along with the sweat. Do you not see that he said that when she sweats in what is below the waist-wrapper, she does not wash it? So he indicated that when she sweats in the place of the waist-wrapper, the predominant circumstance in their case is that there would be najasah there; for this reason he said that she washes it. And that which clarifies this aspect...
ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a menstruating woman make her clothes impure for salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on the sweat of a menstruating woman on her clothing and whether salat (prayer) may be performed in such garments. It indicates that sweat alone does not render the garment problematic, while washing is understood in cases where najasah is likely present together with the sweat.
